+        # Use Sphinx's reader to read the included file, ensuring the
+        # "source-read" event is emitted for the included content.
+        # This allows custom extensions to modify the included file's
+        # content before it is parsed.
+        from sphinx.io import SphinxStandaloneReader
+        from docutils.parsers.rst import directives as rst_directives
+
+        docname = self.env.path2doc(filename)
+        if docname:
+            # Save the current docname and set the included file's docname
+            backup_docname = self.env.docname
+            self.env.temp_data['docname'] = docname
+
+            # Create a SphinxReader and read the included file
+            reader = SphinxStandaloneReader()
+            reader.setup(self.env.app)
+            reader.settings = self.state.document.settings
+
+            # Create a FileInput for the included file
+            from docutils import io as docutils_io
+            source = docutils_io.FileInput(
+                source_path=filename,
+                encoding=self.state.document.settings.input_encoding,
+                error_handler=self.state.document.settings.input_encoding_error_handler,
+            )
+            reader.source = source
+
+            # Call read_source to emit source-read event and get modified content
+            modified_content = reader.read_source(self.env)
+
+            # Restore the docname
+            self.env.temp_data['docname'] = backup_docname
+
+            # Insert the modified content into the parser's input stream
+            from docutils import statemachine
+            include_lines = statemachine.string2lines(
+                modified_content, 
+                self.state.document.settings.tab_width, 
+                convert_whitespace=True
+            )
+            for i, line in enumerate(include_lines):
+                if len(line) > self.state.document.settings.line_length_limit:
+                    raise self.warning(
+                        '"%s": line %d exceeds the line-length-limit.'
+                        % (filename, i + 1)
+                    )
+
+            # Add end of inclusion marker
+            include_lines += ['', '.. end of inclusion from "%s"' % filename]
+            self.state_machine.insert_input(include_lines, filename)
+
+            # Update include-log
+            from docutils import utils
+            include_log = self.state.document.include_log
+            if not include_log:
+                include_log.append((
+                    utils.relative_path(None, self.state.document.current_source), (None, None, None, None)
+                ))
+            clip_options = (None, None, None, None)
+            include_log.append((filename, clip_options))
+
+            return []

+            return super().run()

+"""Test that source-read event modifies included file content."""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def test_include_source_read():
+    """
+    Test that the source-read event is emitted for included files,
+    allowing custom extensions to modify their content.
+    """
+    # Create a temporary directory for the test
+    test_dir = Path("/tmp/sphinx_test_include_source_read")
+    os.makedirs(test_dir)
+
+    try:
+        # Create conf.py
+        conf_py = test_dir / "conf.py"
+        conf_py.write_text("""
+import sys
+import os
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath('.'))
+
+extensions = [
+    'my_extension'
+]
+""")
+
+        # Create my_extension.py
+        ext_py = test_dir / "my_extension.py"
+        ext_py.write_text("""
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+
+from sphinx.application import Sphinx
+
+
+__version__ = '1.0'
+
+
+def subst_vars_replace(app: Sphinx, docname, source):
+    result = source[0]
+    result = result.replace("&REPLACE_ME;", "REPLACED")
+    source[0] = result
+
+
+def setup(app: Sphinx):
+
+    app.connect('source-read', subst_vars_replace)
+
+    return dict(
+        version=__version__,
+        parallel_read_safe=True,
+        parallel_write_safe=True
+    )
+""")
+
+        # Create index.rst
+        index_rst = test_dir / "index.rst"
+        index_rst.write_text("""This is a test
+=============
+
+.. include:: something-to-include.rst
+
+&REPLACE_ME;
+""")
+
+        # Create something-to-include.rst
+        include_rst = test_dir / "something-to-include.rst"
+        include_rst.write_text("""Testing
+=======
+
+&REPLACE_ME;
+""")
+
+        # Run sphinx-build
+        build_dir = test_dir / "build"
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            ["python", "-m", "sphinx", "-b", "html", str(test_dir), str(build_dir)],
+            cwd=str(test_dir),
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+
+        # Check that the build succeeded
+        assert result.returncode == 0, f"Build failed: {result.stderr}"
+
+        # Check that REPLACE_ME is replaced with REPLACED in the output
+        index_html = build_dir / "index.html"
+        index_content = index_html.read_text()
+
+        assert "REPLACE_ME;" not in index_content, \
+            "REPLACE_ME; still present in build output"
+        assert "REPLACED" in index_content, \
+            "REPLACED not found in build output"
+
+        # Check that the replaced content appears twice (once in index.rst, once in included file)
+        assert index_content.count("REPLACED") >= 2, \
+            f"Expected at least 2 REPLACED occurrences, got {index_content.count('REPLACED')}"
+
+        # Check the included file's HTML
+        include_html = build_dir / "something-to-include.html"
+        include_content = include_html.read_text()
+
+        assert "REPLACE_ME;" not in include_content, \
+            "REPLACE_ME; still present in included file HTML"
+        assert "REPLACED" in include_content, \
+            "REPLACED not found in included file HTML"
+
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(test_dir)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    test_include_source_read()
+    print("Test passed!")

judgeRationale:
The agent reimplemented `Include.run()` by reading the file itself via `SphinxStandaloneReader.read_source()` and inserting the raw content into the state machine, bypassing docutils' `BaseInclude.run()` entirely whenever the included file maps to a docname. This drops all of the Include directive's option handling — `:start-line:`, `:end-line:`, `:start-after:`, `:end-before:`, `:literal:`, `:code:`, `:encoding:`, `:parser:`, `:tab-width:`, and the recursion/include-log safeguards. The official fix instead monkey-patches `state_machine.insert_input` so the source-read event fires on the already-clipped text while all native behavior is preserved. The automated tests confirm the regression: for `.. include:: baz/baz.rst :start-line: 4`, the source passed to the handler (and thus inserted into the document) is the entire file (`Baz
===

.. include:: foo.rst

Baz was here.
`) rather than the clipped `
Baz was here.`, meaning the `:start-line:` option is silently ignored and extra content (including a nested include) leaks into the output. It also gates the new path on `path2doc()` returning a docname, so included files outside the source suffixes still don't get the event, and the added test is a subprocess/`/tmp`-based script rather than an integration test in the project's harness (and contains an invalid rST title underline). Existing functionality is broken, so this is not an acceptable fix.
